title: Map of trade routes
subject: History
unit: Summer 1: Medieval peasants and the Black Death (Peasants, Princes & Pestilence)
source: Written for history/y5 lesson 19 (Map of trade routes (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 19: The Black Death, 1348. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

blocks.text: Draw arrows for wool (England to Flanders and Italy), spices and silk (from the east through Constantinople and Cairo to Venice).

model.title: A village of 300: a third die. How many?

keywords.def: a deadly disease that spreads quickly
the plague that swept through Europe and Asia from 1347
tiny living things, some of which cause disease
a tiny jumping insect that bites animals
keeping people apart to stop disease spreading

questions.q: When did the Black Death reach England?
Name one thing people then thought caused it.
questions.a: Bad air, the planets or a punishment

questions.q: Core: Complete a then-and-now table on causes, spread and protection, then answer: 'Why did people then not know the real cause?'
questions.a: Accurate table; answer: no microscopes, germs unknown

questions.q: Extend: Explain why fewer workers after the Black Death mattered for peasants.
questions.a: Workers were scarce, so they could ask for higher wages

questions.q: Stretch: How was the Prophet's teaching about plague like quarantine today?
questions.a: Do not enter or leave a plague land: stay apart to stop the spread

questions.q: We now know the Black Death was caused by:
questions.a: B) Bacteria. Bacteria carried by fleas caused it; the other ideas were medieval beliefs.

questions.q: The Black Death reached England in:
Big question: without germ knowledge, what would you think?
questions.a: Many ideas, like bad air; we now know bacteria and fleas spread it
